title: Neural Mechanisms of Material Perception: Quest on Shitsukan
central_proposition: Material perception, or shitsukan, involves a hierarchical processing of visual information about surface qualities and material properties along the ventral visual pathway, with significant cross-modal integration and the emergence of non-visual material property representations within visual areas.

concept_definitions.name: Shitsukan (質感)
concept_definitions.definition: A Japanese word meaning 'sense of quality', commonly used to cover the wide range of topics related to material perception in a broad sense, including material recognition, surface quality, object appearance, and emotional responses.

concept_definitions.name: Material perception
concept_definitions.definition: Perceiving and recognizing a material category and its properties, surface quality (e.g., glossiness, translucency, texture), or internal state of an object based on sensory stimuli (visual, tactile, auditory).

concept_definitions.name: Surface reflection property
concept_definitions.definition: How light interacts with an object's surface, characterized by components like specular reflection (directional) and diffuse reflection (uniform), and affected by surface roughness.

concept_definitions.name: Glossiness
concept_definitions.definition: A surface quality related to the optical reflection property, influenced by specular and diffuse reflection strengths and the spread of specular reflection due to surface roughness.

concept_definitions.name: Natural textures
concept_definitions.definition: Fine mesostructures with tiny bumps and dents on material surfaces (e.g., bark, leather, fabric) that generate a regular pattern of change in reflected light, providing material-specific information.

concept_definitions.name: Perceptual material properties
concept_definitions.definition: Feelings or impressions about a material evoked by an object's appearance (e.g., hardness, coldness, roughness), measured by subjective ratings.

argument_structure: The paper reviews the current understanding of neural mechanisms for material perception, starting with visual processing of surface qualities (glossiness, natural texture), then material categorization and property recognition, and finally crossmodal interactions. It synthesizes findings from neurophysiological studies in humans and non-human primates to build a comprehensive view of hierarchical processing in the ventral visual pathway and the role of crossmodal learning.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The visual system infers optical properties and mesostructures from retinal images by solving an inverse problem, likely using heuristics and statistical models. This process involves a hierarchical extraction of image features: early visual areas process low-level statistics (e.g., local orientation, spatial frequency, luminance histogram skewness), intermediate areas process higher-order statistics (e.g., correlations), and higher ventral visual areas integrate this information to represent perceptual material properties. Crossmodal interactions occur through learned associations between visual features and non-visual properties (haptic, auditory), which can shape visual representations in the ventral visual cortex itself, allowing non-visual properties to be inferred from visual input.

findings.consequent: Perception and recognition of material category, surface quality, or internal state of an object (material perception/shitsukan)
findings.mechanism: Sensory information is processed and integrated to infer material properties.
findings.quote: Material perception entails perceiving and recognizing a material, surface quality or internal state of an object based on sensory stimuli
findings.empirical_support_cited: Maloney and Brainard, 2010; Fleming et al., 2015a,b

findings.consequent: Appropriate control of actions (e.g., grasping, walking) and decisions (e.g., approach/avoidance, purchase)
findings.mechanism: Perceived material properties inform motor planning and behavioral choices.
findings.quote: Information obtained through material perception can be used to govern actions toward objects and to make decisions

findings.antecedent: Advances in computer graphics (CG) and computer vision technology
findings.consequent: Ability to generate and use stimuli simulating objects with various surface qualities for research
findings.mechanism: Improved simulation and analysis of light-object interaction allows for rigorous experimental control.
findings.quote: Thanks to these advances, it is now possible to generate and use stimuli simulating objects with various surface qualities.

findings.antecedent: Interaction of light in the environment with object's surface mesostructures and optical properties
findings.consequent: Structures within retinal images of objects (image features generating surface qualities)
findings.mechanism: Physical light transport and material properties determine the visual input.
findings.quote: light in the environment interacts with objects having specific surface mesostructures and optical properties to produce various structures within the retinal images

findings.consequent: Inference of optical properties (and mesostructures) by the visual system
findings.mechanism: The visual system solves an inverse, ill-posed problem, likely using heuristics and statistical models, to extract material information from visual input.
findings.source: Physical factors related to surface quality
findings.quote: the visual system infers the optical properties (and mesostructures in the real-world situation) based on a retinal image

findings.antecedent: Simple image statistics (e.g., luminance histogram skewness)
findings.consequent: Cues for estimating optical properties separately from object shape and illumination
findings.mechanism: Specific statistical properties of images correlate with underlying physical material properties.
findings.source: Physical factors related to surface quality
findings.quote: simple image statistics such as luminance histogram provide cues for estimating optical properties separately from other two factors
findings.empirical_support_cited: Motoyoshi et al., 2007; Sharan et al., 2008; Sawayama and Nishida, 2018

findings.antecedent: Differences in patterns of light rays reflected from material surfaces (due to optical properties)
findings.consequent: Differences in visual features in retinal images
findings.mechanism: Material-specific optical properties dictate how light is reflected, forming distinct visual cues.
findings.quote: We can discriminate different materials because the visual features contained in their retinal images differ across materials.

findings.antecedent: Specular reflection (directional) and diffuse reflection (uniform) components of light reflection
findings.consequent: Glossiness of objects
findings.mechanism: The relative strengths and characteristics of these reflection components determine the perceived shininess.
findings.quote: The strengths of the specular and diffuse reflections described above are important physical factors affecting the glossiness of objects.

findings.antecedent: Smoothness or roughness of object surface
findings.consequent: Glossiness of objects
findings.mechanism: Surface irregularities cause variation in the direction of specular reflection, influencing highlight appearance.
findings.quote: Another physical factor affecting glossiness is the smoothness or roughness of the object surface.

findings.antecedent: Object shape and illumination environment (even with constant physical parameters)
findings.consequent: Perceived glossiness of an object
findings.mechanism: These factors influence how highlights appear in the retinal image, which are critical cues for gloss perception.
findings.quote: even when these physical parameters remain constant, the perceived glossiness of an object may change depending on its shape and illumination environment
findings.empirical_support_cited: Fleming et al., 2003; Ho et al., 2008

findings.antecedent: Image features covarying with perceived glossiness (e.g., highlight size, contrast, sharpness, depth)
findings.consequent: Perception of gloss
findings.mechanism: These image features serve as cues for the visual system to infer glossiness.
findings.quote: perception (and misperception) of gloss is well predicted by the way illumination modulates the size, contrast, sharpness, and depth of the highlights.

findings.antecedent: Specular reflection (ps), diffuse reflection (pd), and spread of specular reflection (α)
findings.consequent: Perceived glossiness (contrast gloss, distinctness of gloss)
findings.mechanism: These physical parameters map to perceptual dimensions of gloss, such as highlight contrast and sharpness.
findings.quote: When the basic dimensions of the space that represented perceived gloss were determined using MDS analysis... they identified two axes. One of the axes corresponded to the non-linear combination of the specular and diffuse reflectances (contrast gloss: c) and was interpreted as representing the contrast of the highlights. The other axis (distinctness of gloss: d) corresponded to roughness and was interpreted as representing the sharpness of the highlights.

findings.consequent: Neural representation in the brain
findings.mechanism: Neurons in specific visual cortical areas selectively respond to and encode information about surface reflection properties.
findings.source: Neural responses to gloss: non-human primates
findings.quote: little was known about how information on the surface reflection properties of objects is represented in the brain.

findings.antecedent: Specific combinations of surface reflection parameters (ps, pd, α)
findings.consequent: Selective neuronal responses in the lower bank of the superior temporal sulcus (STS) in macaque IT cortex
findings.mechanism: These 'gloss-selective' neurons encode different aspects of surface reflection.
findings.source: Neural responses to gloss: non-human primates
findings.quote: neurons selectively responsive to specific combinations of these parameters are present in the lower bank of the superior temporal sulcus (STS), in the central part of the IT cortex

findings.consequent: Invariance to changes in 3D shape or illumination environment
findings.mechanism: At this stage of processing, information about surface reflection properties is extracted independently of object shape and illumination.
findings.source: Neural responses to gloss: non-human primates
findings.quote: gloss-selective neurons exhibit invariance to change in the 3D shape of an object or the illumination environment

findings.consequent: Extraction from retinal image and transmission to higher areas (STS) along the ventral pathway
findings.mechanism: Processing begins in early visual areas, likely involving computation of simple image statistics, and progresses hierarchically.
findings.source: Neural responses to gloss: non-human primates
findings.quote: the extraction of information about surface reflection properties starts from the early stage, and the information is sent to the higher area in the STS along the ventral pathway.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Okazawa et al., 2012; Motoyoshi et al., 2007

findings.consequent: Strong fMRI responses along the human ventral visual pathway (early visual areas to higher areas)
findings.mechanism: Visual processing of gloss engages a hierarchical network in the ventral stream.
findings.quote: Wada et al. (2014) showed in human fMRI experiments that strong responses to images of glossy objects were observed along the ventral visual pathway from early visual areas to higher areas.

findings.consequent: Activation of hV4, VO-2, and V3A/B in the right hemisphere
findings.mechanism: These areas play important roles in top-down modulation of gloss perception.
findings.quote: When the subjects paid attention to the glossiness, only hV4, VO-2 and V3A/B in the right hemisphere were activated

findings.consequent: Linear representation of perceptual gloss parameters (contrast gloss, distinctness of gloss)
findings.mechanism: Neuronal activity directly encodes the perceptual attributes of highlights.
findings.source: Perceptual attributes of glossiness: neural representation
findings.quote: the responses of these neurons changed linearly across the space delineated by the c and d axes and could be well represented as a linear combination of c and d.

findings.consequent: High precision estimation of perceptual gloss parameters
findings.mechanism: The collective response of these neurons contains sufficient information to decode perceived gloss.
findings.source: Perceptual attributes of glossiness: neural representation
findings.quote: the perceptual gloss parameters of the stimuli (c and d) could be estimated with high precision based on the activities of the population of gloss-selective neurons.

findings.antecedent: Natural textures (e.g., fabric, fur, stone, bark, leather)
findings.consequent: Material-specific patterns of light reflection (due to bumps, dents, fiber structures, woven patterns, material components)
findings.mechanism: Mesoscopic surface structures and optical properties create unique light reflection patterns that are diagnostic of material identity.
findings.quote: Many materials such as fabric, fur, stone, bark and leather have specific natural textures with bumps and dents, and they are useful for classification of materials.

findings.antecedent: Image statistics (local orientations, spatial frequencies, higher-order correlations)
findings.consequent: Processing of natural textures
findings.mechanism: The visual system extracts and processes these statistical properties to represent texture information.
findings.quote: some form of image statistics plays an important role in the processing of natural textures.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Heeger and Bergen, 1995; Portilla and Simoncelli, 2000; Varma and Zisserman, 2005

findings.antecedent: Naturalistic synthesized texture images (containing higher-order statistics)
findings.consequent: Stronger responses in macaque V2 neurons compared to noise-like textures (only Gabor-like filters)
findings.mechanism: V2 neurons are sensitive to higher-order image statistics beyond simple local orientation and spatial frequency.
findings.source: Neural processing of natural texture: non-human primates
findings.quote: V2 neurons showed stronger responses to the naturalistic synthesized texture images... but V1 neurons do not.

findings.consequent: Gradual advancement through extraction of higher-order image statistics along the ventral pathway (V2 to V4)
findings.mechanism: The hierarchy of the ventral stream progressively extracts more complex statistical features of textures.
findings.source: Neural processing of natural texture: non-human primates
findings.quote: This reflects the gradual advancement of the texture processing through extraction of higher order image statistics along the hierarchy of the ventral pathway.

findings.consequent: More responsive human V2-V4 areas compared to noise-like textures
findings.mechanism: Human early and mid-level visual areas are sensitive to higher-order image statistics of natural textures.
findings.source: Neural processing of natural texture: humans
findings.quote: Freeman et al. (2013) used fMRI to show that in humans areas V2-V4 are more responsive to naturalistic synthesized textures than to noise-like textures

findings.consequent: Processing in the medial part of the human ventral visual cortex (around the collateral sulcus, CoS)
findings.mechanism: This region is functionally specialized for texture processing, largely independent of object shape processing.
findings.source: Neural processing of natural texture: humans
findings.quote: information about natural texture is processed in the medial part of the ventral visual cortex around the CoS largely independently of object shape information
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cant and Goodale, 2007; Cant et al., 2009; Cavina-Pratesi et al., 2010a,b; Sathian et al., 2011; Podrebarac et al., 2014

findings.consequent: Joint sensitivity in medial ventral visual cortex regions (overlapping with PPA)
findings.mechanism: This region computes image statistics features relevant to both texture and scene perception (gist).
findings.source: Functional map in the human ventral visual cortex
findings.quote: regions selective to natural texture in the medial part overlap with a scene-selective sub-region called the parahippocampal place area (PPA), and this region is sensitive to object ensembles
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cant and Xu, 2012, 2015, 2016; Lowe et al., 2017; Oliva, 2005

findings.consequent: Response selectivity for both natural texture and shape
findings.mechanism: This region integrates information about texture and shape, potentially forming integrated object representations.
findings.source: Functional map in the human ventral visual cortex
findings.quote: the FG region lateral to the CoS and medial to the shape-selective LO often exhibits response selectivity for both natural texture and shape
findings.empirical_support_cited: Cant and Goodale, 2007; Cant et al., 2009; Cavina-Pratesi et al., 2010b

findings.antecedent: Visual information about optical properties (gloss) and natural texture
findings.consequent: Estimation of material category and its properties by the visual system
findings.mechanism: These visual cues are diagnostic for material identification.
findings.source: RECOGNITION OF MATERIAL CATEGORY AND ITS PROPERTIES
findings.quote: The visual system likely uses such information to estimate the material category and its properties.

findings.consequent: Decoding from fMRI activity patterns in early, middle, and higher-order visual areas
findings.mechanism: Information about material category is distributed across the visual hierarchy.
findings.quote: viewed material categories can be decoded statistically significantly from the activities in early, middle, and higher order visual areas.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Hiramatsu et al., 2011; Jacobs et al., 2014

findings.consequent: Decoding from ERP patterns as early as 100 ms after stimulus onset
findings.mechanism: Early visual areas are involved in rapid material categorization.
findings.quote: wood and stone material categories could be decoded based on the patterns of ERPs as early as 100 ms after stimulus onset.

findings.consequent: Higher activity around the CoS in human ventral visual cortex compared to 3D shape discrimination
findings.mechanism: The CoS is specialized for processing material category information.
findings.quote: activity in the ventral visual cortex around the CoS (Fig. 6, blue circle) is higher during discrimination of material category (wood vs rock) than during discrimination of a 3D shape

findings.consequent: Accurate estimation of nonvisual properties (e.g., microscale roughness, hardness, coldness, weight)
findings.mechanism: Humans learn associations between visual features and nonvisual properties through experience.
findings.quote: humans can accurately estimate such nonvisual properties from the visual appearance of materials, in a way that correlates with those haptically estimated through touching them

findings.antecedent: Neural similarity in human V1/V2 activity patterns for material categories
findings.consequent: Correlation with similarities in low-level image features
findings.mechanism: Early visual areas represent material categories based on their basic visual features.
findings.quote: the neural similarities between material categories obtained from early visual areas (V1/V2) are well correlated with similarities in low-level image features

findings.antecedent: Neural similarity in human higher-order ventral visual cortex (FG/CoS) activity patterns for material categories
findings.consequent: Reliable correlation with similarity of perceptual material properties
findings.mechanism: Higher visual areas represent material categories in terms of their perceived properties.
findings.quote: the neural similarity obtained from a higher order area in the human ventral visual cortex... reliably correlates with similarity of perceptual material properties

findings.consequent: Gradual transformation from low-level features (V1/V2) to perceptual material properties (higher areas)
findings.mechanism: The ventral visual pathway performs a hierarchical abstraction of material information.
findings.quote: representation in mid-level areas V3/V4 was between those in V1/V2 and FG/COS... image-based representation of material categories in V1/V2 is gradually transformed through V3/V4 into a representation more reflective of the perceptual material properties in the higher area.

findings.antecedent: Human ventral visual cortex (around CoS and FG)
findings.consequent: Activity reflecting non-visual material properties
findings.mechanism: This region integrates visual information with learned associations of non-visual properties.
findings.quote: the ventral visual cortex in humans exhibits activity reflecting some non-visual material properties.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Hiramatsu et al., 2011; Cant and Goodale, 2011; Gallivan et al., 2014

findings.consequent: Decoding from activity in early visual areas (V1-V3)
findings.mechanism: Decoding is based on low-level image features and PS statistics.
findings.quote: roughness and texturedness can be decoded from activity in the early visual areas (V1-V3), and their decoding is likely based to a considerable extent on low-level image features and PS statistics.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Baumgartner and Gegenfurtner, 2016; Ho et al., 2006; Giesel and Zaidi, 2013

findings.consequent: Decoding only from activity in the lingual gyrus (LG), medial part of the ventral cortex
findings.mechanism: Specific higher ventral visual areas are involved in representing nonvisual material properties.
findings.quote: hardness, a nonvisual property, could be decoded only from activity in the LG, the medial part of the ventral cortex

findings.antecedent: Early and higher ventral visual areas
findings.consequent: Emergence of visual and nonvisual material property representations
findings.mechanism: The visual hierarchy processes different aspects of material properties, from basic visual features to abstract perceptual qualities, including those inferred crossmodally.
findings.quote: These findings... indicate representation of visual and nonvisual material properties emerge in early and higher ventral visual areas, respectively.

findings.antecedent: Material information processing in human and nonhuman primates
findings.consequent: Interspecies commonality in neural architecture
findings.mechanism: The neural architecture for visual material processing has been shaped through evolution.
findings.quote: Overall, the results indicate an interspecies commonality in neural architecture for visual material information processing, which suggests that to a large extent the architecture has been shaped through evolution.

findings.antecedent: Perceiving a material through multiple sensory modalities (e.g., seeing and touching an object)
findings.consequent: Processing of information derived from each modality within respective sensory cortices and appropriate integration
findings.mechanism: Sensory cortices, while largely independent, can interact and integrate information.
findings.quote: When perceiving a material through multiple sensory modalities... the information derived from each modality is processed within the respective sensory cortices and appropriately integrated.

findings.consequent: Dependence on color
findings.mechanism: Crossmodal interactions influence perception, where one sensory modality affects another.
findings.quote: somatosensory perception of temperature changes depends on color (e.g., Ho et al., 2014)

findings.consequent: Dependence on visual texture ('material-weight illusion')
findings.mechanism: Crossmodal interactions influence perception, where one sensory modality affects another.
findings.quote: haptic weight changes depending on visual texture ('material-weight illusion', Buckingham et al., 2009).

findings.consequent: Affected by haptic slipperiness of a surface
findings.mechanism: Crossmodal interactions influence perception, where one sensory modality affects another.
findings.quote: visual glossiness can be affected by the haptic slipperiness of a surface (Adams et al., 2016).

findings.consequent: Changes in perceptual material properties
findings.mechanism: Crossmodal interactions influence perception, where one sensory modality affects another.
findings.quote: audiovisual interactions in which perceptual material properties change depending on the combination of visual appearance and sounds

findings.consequent: Increased activity in somatosensory cortex and visual cortex (medial part of ventral visual cortex, earlier areas)
findings.mechanism: Haptic processing recruits visual areas, suggesting crossmodal integration.
findings.quote: during the haptic texture judgment, activity is increased not only in the somatosensory cortex but also within the visual cortex
findings.empirical_support_cited: Stilla and Sathian, 2008; Sathian et al., 2011; Podrebarac et al., 2014

findings.consequent: Stronger response in medial part of the ventral visual cortex compared to other classes of sounds (e.g., voice)
findings.mechanism: Visual areas are recruited for processing material-related auditory information, indicating crossmodal links.
findings.quote: the medial part of the ventral visual cortex responds more strongly to the sounds of various materials than to other classes of sounds such as a voice

findings.antecedent: Congruent visual and haptic bimodal texture stimulation
findings.consequent: Enhanced activity in a portion of the visual cortex (CoS, earlier visual areas)
findings.mechanism: Crossmodal congruence facilitates processing in visual areas.
findings.quote: a portion of the visual cortex, including the region around the CoS and earlier visual areas, are enhanced by the addition of haptic texture stimulation, especially when congruent between modalities.

findings.antecedent: Simple feature differences in haptic texture (e.g., inter-dot interval)
findings.consequent: Decoding from activity in early visual areas
findings.mechanism: Early visual areas process basic haptic features.
findings.quote: simple feature differences in haptic texture (i.e., inter-dot interval) can be decoded from activity in early visual areas

findings.antecedent: Perceptual roughness of haptic texture (not simply inter-dot interval)
findings.consequent: Decoding from activity around the CoS
findings.mechanism: Higher visual areas (CoS) process more complex perceptual aspects of haptic texture.
findings.quote: perceptual roughness of the haptic texture (which is not related simply to the inter-dot interval) can be decoded from activity around the CoS.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation with images affording micro/meso-scale surface properties
findings.consequent: Automatic recruitment of the somatosensory cortex
findings.mechanism: Visual input can automatically activate somatosensory representations due to learned associations.
findings.quote: the somatosensory cortex can be automatically recruited by visual stimulation with images that afford micro/meso-scale surface properties

findings.antecedent: Visuo-tactile texture matching task (requiring comparison across modalities)
findings.consequent: Higher activities in SPL, lateral PFC, MTL, and ventral visual cortex (FG/CoS) compared to visuo-tactile orientation matching
findings.mechanism: Multisensory and memory-related areas are involved in active crossmodal comparison of material properties.
findings.quote: activities in the SPL, lateral PFC, MTL and ventral visual cortex around the FG and CoS were higher during a visuo-tactile texture matching task than during a visuo-tactile orientation matching task.

findings.consequent: Increased activity in the precuneus
findings.mechanism: The precuneus is involved in detecting and processing crossmodal mismatches.
findings.quote: the activity in the precuneus increased when the visual and tactile textures were incongruent.

findings.antecedent: Learned associations between information from different modalities (e.g., material appearance, touch, sound)
findings.consequent: Crossmodal interactions
findings.mechanism: Daily multimodal experiences create correspondences that shape sensory processing.
findings.quote: It has often been considered that crossmodal interactions reflect associations between information from different modalities
findings.empirical_support_cited: Beauchamp et al., 2004; Spence, 2011; Smith and Goodale, 2015; Ernst, 2007; Seitz et al., 2007; Flanagan et al., 2008

findings.consequent: Brain learns correspondences between material appearance, touch, and sound
findings.mechanism: Repeated exposure to multimodal cues leads to the formation of crossmodal associations.
findings.quote: In handling objects made of various materials in everyday life, the brain learns correspondences between the appearance of the material and its touch and sound
findings.empirical_support_cited: Abe et al., 2012; Schwartz and Nishino, 2013; Yuan et al., 2017; Owens et al., 2016

findings.antecedent: Task-relevant, learned, visual-haptic associations (e.g., object weight with texture)
findings.consequent: Decoding from texture-selective region in ventral visual cortex (CoS)
findings.mechanism: Learned crossmodal associations are flexibly represented within visual areas, allowing visual cues to activate non-visual property representations.
findings.quote: learned, visual-haptic associations are not only stored in certain memory-related and/or multisensory areas such as the MTL, but also flexibly represented at the level of the visual cortex.

findings.antecedent: Simple visuo-haptic exposure to real-world materials
findings.consequent: Alteration of material representation in macaque PIT (ventral visual cortex) to better reflect visual and haptic material properties
findings.mechanism: Multimodal experience shapes visual representations, enabling them to acquire crossmodal associations and represent non-visual properties.
findings.quote: material representation in the PIT, part of ventral visual cortex, is altered by this simple visuo-haptic exposure. Through exposure, the representation in that region came to more reflect the visual and haptic material properties

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Investigate the temporal aspects of neural processes underlying material perception using high temporal resolution techniques (e.g., single neuron recordings, EEG, magnetoencephalography).
Examine the causal relationships between neuronal activities representing specific material properties/surface qualities and perception/behavior using artificial manipulation of neural activities.
Study the neural substrates of the evaluation of objects/scenes and emotional responses to materials, as this area is currently under-researched.
bridge_warrants: Material perception is tightly linked to object recognition and scene perception, leveraging similar hierarchical processing in the ventral visual pathway.
The visual system's inference of optical properties from retinal images is framed as an 'inverse problem' from computer vision, solved using heuristics and statistical models.
The concept of 'image statistics' (e.g., luminance histogram skewness, higher-order correlations) bridges early visual processing to computational models of material perception.
Crossmodal interactions in material perception are explained by 'learned associations' between sensory modalities, linking to memory systems and multisensory integration frameworks.
The functional organization of the ventral visual cortex for material and shape processing is compared across human and nonhuman primates, suggesting evolutionary conservation.
methodological_critiques: The physical processes leading to sensory signals related to material perception are complicated, making it difficult to manipulate experimental stimuli rigorously.
Experiments involving Portilla and Simoncelli (PS) statistics for texture synthesis are technically challenging due to the large number of parameters and possible texture images.

Decoding performance in fMRI for material categorization may depend on the spatial organization of category-sensitive neurons (e.g., uniform vs. orderly arrangement), requiring complementary methods for conclusive assessment.
There is still little known about the temporal aspects of the neural processes underlying material perception.
Little research has been conducted on the neural substrates of emotional responses and preference/aversion related to material perception.
model_structure: The paper proposes a conceptual model (Fig. 1) illustrating 'Shitsukan' perception as a process where physical properties (object, scene, optical, surface mesostructure) lead to sensory stimulation, which undergoes neural processing to result in perception of material/surface quality (glossiness, natural texture, material category/property), ultimately influencing preference/aversion, emotional response, approach/avoidance, and motor control. It also presents a conceptual mapping (Fig. 8) showing how material representation transforms from low-level image properties in early visual areas to perceptual material properties in higher ventral visual areas in both human and macaque brains.
limitations: The temporal aspects of neural processes underlying material perception are not well understood.
The causal relationships between neuronal activities and material perception/behavior need further investigation through artificial manipulation of neural activities.
Research on the neural substrates of emotional responses and preference/aversion related to material perception is limited.
The functional differences between texture/material-related regions along the CoS, particularly between posterior and anterior parts, are not fully understood.
The specific image features to which macaque IT cortex neurons respond for natural textures remain unresolved.
The neural mechanisms related to the perception of transparency and translucency are not well understood.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: A new conceptual framework is proposed to explain the neural mechanisms underlying the perception and recognition of material qualities (shitsukan) from multisensory input.

mechanism_chain.description: Causal mechanism describing the neural processing stages from multisensory input to the perception of material qualities (shitsukan).

steps.to_construct: Early sensory processing in modality-specific cortices
Feature extraction and integration in higher-order sensory areas
